query: What business models and customers do these companies describe?

per_column.name: primary_business_model
per_column.rationale: The business model (how the company creates and captures value) is a core constitutive aspect of a company's business profile.

per_column.name: primary_customer_segment
per_column.rationale: Who the customers are is an explicit part of the query and a genuine aspect OF the business profile.

per_column.name: service_delivery_mode
per_column.rationale: How the offering is delivered (SaaS, on-prem, hardware) is a distinct aspect of the profile, though it partially correlates with business model.

per_column.name: industry_focus
per_column.rationale: The industry/domain a company operates in is a constitutive aspect of its business profile.

per_column.name: value_proposition_type
per_column.rationale: The type of value delivered is an aspect OF the business profile describing what the company offers to customers.

judge.rationale: All five columns are genuine part-of aspects of a company_business_profile rather than external predictors or causes, satisfying the meronymy requirement. Mutual exclusivity is good but not perfect: business_model, service_delivery_mode, and industry_focus overlap substantially (e.g. 'software_platform' business model correlates heavily with 'cloud_saas' delivery and 'software_development' industry; value categories like 'security_compliance' echo the 'cybersecurity' industry). This shared underlying dimension of 'what kind of software/product company it is' reduces non-overlap. Exhaustiveness is strong for the query's stated scope (business models + customers): it covers model, customer, delivery, industry, and value proposition. Minor gaps include revenue/monetization mechanics and company scale/stage, which are also constitutive aspects of a full business profile but are not decomposed here.
